properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-12, watching the session's tool tally read "7 tools used (1 failed)": *"I want to be able to come back to this failure to make sure we understand what happened and why it failed, but sometimes mid-task I feel we are focused on the task and this failure is never revisited."*

THE INSTANCE HE WAS LOOKING AT: `add_decision` refused by the search-first guard (a Decision and a DesignRule read close to the idea being written); the agent judged both distinct and resent with `distinct_from`. A guard working as designed — and still a failure nobody would have written down. It is the fifteenth near-match refusal on the record and the fifteenth judged distinct (`fact:twelve-near-match-refusals-across-two-designs-and-not-one-was-a-duplicate` counted fourteen on 2026-08-31), and that count only exists because agents self-reported.

═══ WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY HOLDS ═══

· `rule:an-identified-issue-is-enduring-never-dropped` (his word, 2026-08-20): before moving on, an identified issue is a durable node, an asked Question with a name on it, or a computed finding that fires again — never only a sentence in a conversation. The rule exists; what it lacks is a moment. Mid-task, "before moving on" is exactly the moment the agent is least likely to stop.
· `record_finding` writes a dated observation on the node it concerns, in one call. `report_manual_work` records hand-rolled work with a closed diagnosis. Both are the right durable form; both depend on the agent noticing and choosing to call them while focused on something else — the same dependency that left the near-match count unmeasured until users reported it.
· `req:detecting-is-not-asking` gives the shape: record unconditionally at the moment, invite attention at a boundary (capture-session, an increment close, a `loop_status` read).

═══ THE IDEAS, WITH COSTS AND COUNTERS ═══

A. ⭐ THE SERVER KEEPS ITS OWN REFUSAL LEDGER. reflow2 is the one that issued the refusal; it does not need the agent to remember. Every refusal a session meets (which tool, which guard, what it said) is tallied by the server and surfaced at a boundary: `loop_status` / capture-session says "this session met 4 refusals: 3 near-match (judged distinct), 1 missing-argument — revisit?". Zero agent effort, works for any project and any agent, and it is the only option that captures the failure the agent did NOT notice. COUNTER: it sees only reflow2's own refusals. A `gh` error, a shell pipe, a CI red are outside its sight. And a tally is a detection, not an understanding — "why it failed" still needs a person or an agent to look, which is the boundary's job.

B. A ONE-WORD PARK. A single cheap call — or a flag on any tool call — meaning "this failed, come back to it": lands a Question or a finding with the failure text attached and nobody's name yet, so the enduring-issue rule is satisfied in one motion instead of a judgement. COUNTER: still requires the agent to make the call mid-task, which is the behaviour being measured as unreliable; cheaper than today, not automatic.

C. A FAILURE IS A GAP THE LOOP OWES. Treat an unrevisited refusal like an unsurfaced gap: it counts in `loop_status` until somebody dispositions it (guard-working / real-defect / unexplained), the way drift needs a disposition. Makes the failure impossible to skim past. COUNTER: a guard that works correctly fires often (14 of 14 near-match refusals were the guard being right), so without A's tally to feed it and a cheap "guard working" disposition, this becomes noise that teaches the reader to acknowledge in bulk — the exact erosion the two-sided accept forbids.

D. THE HARNESS-SIDE HOOK. A Stop/PostToolUse hook that notices a failed reflow2 call and nudges, as the existing Stop hook nudges for `loop_status`. COUNTER: harness-specific (Claude Code only), which fails his "any agent/model" scope; and the nudge is prose again.

═══ WHERE IT LEANS (a finding, not a decision) ═══

A first, because it is the only one that costs the agent nothing and catches what the agent did not notice; C on top of A so a refusal is dispositioned rather than merely counted; B as the manual form for failures outside reflow2's sight (shell, git, CI), where the agent is the only witness. Not D. And the disposition vocabulary matters more than the tally: "guard working" must be one word, or the ledger becomes a list nobody reads.
properties.name: OPEN — when a tool call fails mid-task, how does that failure get revisited instead of lost to the task at hand?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill mid-session, while PR #489 is in CI; nothing built. A separate node from the notepad idea because it is a different question — that one asks where a LESSON lives and whether an agent reads it; this asks how a FAILURE survives the moment it happens. The two meet: a notepad has nothing to say about failures nobody revisited.
